observation.visible_scene: A close-up, roughly centered view of a transparent spherical snow globe containing a small Santa Claus figurine that holds a star-shaped object. The globe and figure sit against a dark background punctuated by large out-of-focus colored light blobs (red, green, blue, orange). The scene is dominated by the figurine's illuminated face and beard, the star in its hands, and bright specular highlights/reflections on the glass surface.
visible_changes: The dominant hue of the light bathing the globe alternates in regular blocks between a purple/magenta cast and an orange/red cast across the excerpt (purple in early frames, orange in a middle block, repeating several times), indicating a cycling color light source rather than a one-time change.

The background bokeh blobs shift color and brightness in step with the globe's lighting (e.g., a red top-left blob and green bottom-right blob in purple-lit frames, a blue top-left blob in some orange-lit frames), and small internal reflections/highlights on the glass move and change color accordingly.
The Santa figurine's pose, orientation, and position inside the globe remain unchanged throughout; no rotation, translation, or deformation of the figure is visible.
Tiny suspended specks (glitter/snow) inside the globe show no clear coordinated swirling or settling motion over the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: The mechanism and full period of the color cycling (whether it continues, pauses, or changes pattern beyond this segment).
Whether the globe rests on a rotating or vibrating base, and any motion before t=0 or after the last frame.
The physical source and placement of the colored lights behind/inside the globe.
uncertain_details: Whether there is slight camera shake or only lighting-driven apparent shifts; the globe's framing stays nearly constant but minor jitter cannot be fully separated from illumination changes.
Whether the green arc reflection on the left of the globe is a separate light or a reflection of the background bokeh.
Any very slow drift of the internal specks is not confidently distinguishable from compression noise.

background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
